chunks: Indeed, a man will appear among you after me, broad-throated and pot-bellied,
He will eat whatever he finds and crave what he does not find. Kill him, but you will not kill him!
Know that he will command you to curse me and to renounce me;
As for cursing, curse me, for it is purification for me and salvation for you;
As for renunciation, do not renounce me, for I was born upon the natural disposition, and I was foremost in faith and migration.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the ruler mentioned in Nahj al-Balagha and the Prophet's instruction regarding his curse?
ai.summary: This famous hadith from Nahj al-Balagha identifies Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan as the 'swallowing' ruler, using the metaphor of gluttony to denote his insatiable appetite for power and wealth. The Prophet’s instruction to 'curse him' (sab) while 'not disowning him' (bara') highlights the Shia distinction between political opposition and spiritual lineage, affirming that despite his usurpation, Muawiya remained within the fold of Islam by virtue of the Prophet’s innate fitrah and early faith. This passage underscores the concept of 'waiting' (intizar) for the true Imam while enduring the political reality of the Umayyad caliphate.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Soon after me there would be put on you a man with a broad mouth and a big belly.
He would swallow whatever he gets and would crave for what he does not get. You should kill him but (I know) you would not kill him.
He would command you to abuse me and to renounce me.
As for abusing, you do abuse me because that would mean purification for me and salvation for you.

As regards renunciation, you should not renounce me because I have been born on the natural religion (Islam) and was foremost in (accepting) it as well as in Hijrah (migrating from Mecca to Medina). [1]
